purpose: Evidence inventory for the Khafre ground constraint. Coordinates are latitude north and longitude east. A plotted section, a regional anomaly and a local residual answer different questions.
scope: Search bounded to the named public archives, publications, and author/project sources below. An unlocated or unpublished local survey could change the result. No paid downloads or correspondence. Independent fields were collected before the 2025 claim.

sources.title: Khafre Project, conference abstract, March 16, 2025
sources.coverage: Eight hollow cylindrical structures with spiral routes in two north-south rows. The document places the bottom at 648 m below its ground zero. No surveyed shaft axes, inner-radius values, roof elevations, density measurements or dimensional error bars were tabulated.

sources.title: Project conference annotated slide and Biondi interview
sources.coverage: The conference slide uses a 20 m tube diameter as an assumption (companion depth branch). The January 23, 2026 interview discusses a 20 m column diameter. Neither establishes measured inner void radius. Model tests filled cross-sections of 2, 5 and 10 m radius.

sources.title: Project catalog and independent approximate base elevation
sources.coverage: Project catalog targets are longitude, latitude. Khafre 31.1308, 29.9761. Khufu 31.134186, 29.979175. Nell and Ruggles, table 12, gives a rough elevation of 69 m for Khafre. Elevation estimates mix GPMP control points and Google Earth. These define regional calculations only.

sources.title: Riad / Assiut University contributors, NOAA NGDC Egypt gravity stations
sources.dates: Received March 1989, 1999 edition. No dates of individual occupations or uncertainty fields in the distributed station table.
sources.coverage: 71 irregular station records. Exact data listing includes coordinates, level elevation, observed gravity, simple Bouguer and free-air anomalies. No terrain adjustment. Values reference IGSN71, anomalies GRS67. This is station data, not a grid. Nearest point and conditional prediction are computed from the raw file.

sources.title: BGI public land-gravity map and survey metadata, British Antarctic Survey and E. Tengstrom
sources.coverage: Two public location features in a roughly 6 by 6 km square around the catalog center. Snapshot primary keys match survey metadata. These are map coordinates of limited precision. Altitudes are null and no g or uncertainty fields are served. Dates are compilation dates. Full relative-data delivery is a separate request-based service. Public catalog metadata are distinct from station observations.

sources.title: G. Dawod, The Egyptian National Gravity Standardization Network (ENGSN97), Fig. 2
sources.coverage: Original card visually read: station SRI 1, Giza City, 30°00′10″ N, 31°10′50″ E, 19 m above mean sea level; unadjusted 979300 mGal printed. The April 1997 FG5 absolute stations used GPS and precise leveling. National network mean separation 67 km. Adjusted network uncertainties span 2 to 48 microgal, mean 21, without a site-specific uncertainty on this card. One city station cannot define a pyramid residual. Dawod, 1998 doctoral dissertation, printed page 118: the absolute observation at SRI1 has estimated standard deviation 0.005 mGal (5 microgal). This is the uncertainty used for the city-station sensitivity comparison.

sources.title: Al-Krargy and Dawod, Egypt unified terrestrial gravity database, 2026
sources.coverage: 9,724 records from diverse networks and survey lines. Its authors say the data belong to Egypt's Survey Research Institute and may be available upon request. No near-Khafre station table supplied by the paper. Coverage, uncertainty and station spacing at the target cannot be inferred from the national count.

sources.title: Lakshmanan and Montlucon, Microgravity probes the Great Pyramid, 1987; Operation Kheops 1986
sources.coverage: Actual local profiles at Khufu. Two Queen's passage profiles include 46 stations spaced 0.5-2 m. In the separate boat-pit test, 35 readings 1-6 m apart yielded lows of 30-50 microgal. Local elevation, pyramid, known openings, granite and terrain were considered in the interior analysis. Reported repeat differences about 5 microgal in the French account. Published maps and lines, no coordinate/elevation/gravity station table identified in these reports. Khufu's center is about 473 m from Khafre. A regional Bouguer profile through Khufu in the French Fig. 12 is on a 50 km scale. Neither set is a corrected near-field grid surrounding Khafre.

sources.title: Moussa, Dolphin and Mokhtar, Applications of Modern Sensing Techniques to Egyptology, 1977 field experiments
sources.coverage: Downward soundings at 11 positions in the Belzoni chamber area and passage. Fig. 92 gives a relative plan with a 5 m scale. Fig. 93 pools picked slant ranges at 9, 21 and 33 m, with numerical ticks from 5 to 40 m. Fig. 95 reconstructs arcs of possible reflector locations. The team considered both geological and chamber explanations. Their one-way calibration gives 19.8 m in 6.6 ms; their independent two-way check agreed within 6%. That agreement is not a formal uncertainty. They separately estimated about 10% local range error on the west pavement, not a chamber-specific depth interval.
sources.instrument: Section IV.D.2 describes long-range use as 'up to 50 m in rock'. Electrical drive pulse 0.13-1.3 ms, longer acoustic pulse under ringing. Period between shots 100 ms. A-scope interpulse range 150 m for the assumed sound speed. Receiver and sync went to two-channel tape. Neither total tape duration, usable receiver time for each floor shot, nor full per-station floor waveform durations are reported. Published floor figure is a histogram. No raw floor tapes linked from author report or index. Numbers cannot be read as a maximum explored depth or as a 648 m non-detection.

sources.title: Abbas et al., Uncovering the Pyramids-Giza Plateau, 2012
sources.coverage: February 2006 GPR survey. Khafre zone 2: P24 and P25, each 210 m long, 2 m apart. P25 placed 10 m from the base. Site maps and processed profiles are available. No under-footprint deep array, open numerical traces or 648 m sensitivity calibration supplied in the paper.

sources.title: Sharafeldin et al., groundwater surveys, 2019
sources.coverage: Fig. 4 locates 10 electrical, 26 seismic and 19 GPR profiles at selected plateau sites, including the causeway. Electrical spacing 5 m, electrode elevations incorporated in inversion. Seismic geophones at 5 m with 115 m spread. Near-surface aquifers, geological heterogeneity and tens-of-metres target depths. Paper published February 2019; field dates of the individual profiles not stated here. Raw data available from author upon request. No tested deep-shaft target.

sources.title: Alvarez et al., Science 1970, and ScIDEP collaboration 2025
sources.coverage: Real 1967-onward Khafre cosmic-ray experiment observed density along downward muons' paths above Belzoni's chamber. Its chamber-sized exclusion cone lies above the detector. The 2025 instrumentation paper concerns the pyramid interior. Neither supplies trajectories through the rock 648 m below the chamber.

sources.title: Hemeda and Sonbol, Sustainability problems of the Giza pyramids, Table 10 (2020)
sources.coverage: Khafre backing-block samples: 2.31, 2.29 and 2.25 g/cm³ in the unit-weight column (given in density units). Local material analog only. No borehole density profile to 648 m. The 2300 kg/m³ constant used here is a model input. 2000-2600 kg/m³ is an exploratory bracket, not a measured local interval.

sources.title: Smallwood, The attraction of the pyramids, 2018
sources.coverage: Regional NGDC values and computed local topographic effects. Deflection-of-the-vertical profiles are modeled. The paper notes public gravity samples were too far apart to resolve proposed stations 85 m from the Khufu crest. Its 2200/2500 kg/m³ terrain assumptions and 2300 kg/m³ Egypt Bouguer reduction contextualize the scenario density.

sources.title: BGI World Gravity Map 2012, and Hirt et al. GGMplus 2013
sources.coverage: WGM2012 2 arc-minute output samples are about 3.7 km north-south by 3.2 km east-west at Giza. Underlying EGM2008/DTU10 with 1 arc-minute ETOPO1 terrain terms. GGMplus has about 200 m grid spacing, but below about 10 km its short-scale signal is computed from relief with an assumed density. Sampling a point above Khafre in either model does not create a local field observation.

sources.title: ESA GOCE mission specifications
sources.coverage: Approximately 100 km spatial scale with gravity-anomaly accuracy target of 1 mGal (1000 microgal). Direct space gravimetry is distinct from modeled terrain refinements and local gravimeter readings.

sources.title: USGS techniques for repeat gravity surveys; EPA gravity method
sources.coverage: USGS nominal free-air gradient -3.086 microgal/cm. A free-air anomaly corrects the effect of station elevation relative to a reference. A simple Bouguer anomaly also removes a modeled slab and still lacks detailed terrain and monument corrections. A test requires station-level readings and consistent reductions. Regional anomalies can coexist with local sources of either sign.

sources.title: Eight positions digitized by companion depth audit from conference slide 76
sources.coverage: The marks are annotations on a perspective-corrected diagram. They are not surveyed shaft coordinates. Used only to see how the near-field prediction varies with the published arrangement. Bearings are unnecessary because the four separate comparisons use the rectified square axes.

sources.title: Brown, Girdler and Renner, A gravity traverse across northern Africa, 1980
sources.coverage: The primary abstract reports 608 readings on the trans-African 1975 expedition. The checked record does not supply a local station series across Khafre.
